description: del Val, Laura and colleagues publish this resource through Zenodo. The implemented simulation couples a one-dimensional unsaturated-zone HYDRUS calculation through Phydrus with a two-dimensional saturated-zone groundwater model through FloPy. Leakage from the first model becomes recharge and pollutant input to the second. The source explicitly assumes linear sorption and a static groundwater level, excluding drying and rewetting effects. It is intended as an initial PFOS fate-and-transport approximation when information is limited. This differs from the separately described transient three-dimensional coupled train. Native model-package terms are CC-BY, while its current public repository is labelled MIT. Coverage is limited to the stated models, observations and application settings. Native metadata gives open access and the licence label cc-by-4.0. These terms describe the deposit; software and companion-data terms are distinguished where separately established. Only descriptive metadata and file descriptors were inspected; linked data, code and document bodies were not opened.
